reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify potential spurious features through cross-instance pattern recognition with XAI tools to quantitatively validate feature importance and detect shared high-attribution patterns. This approach ensures both pattern-level intuition and statistical rigor in pinpointing spurious correlations that are not semantically meaningful but drive misclassification. Given that all instances are misclassified and feature-level spuriousness is suspected, combining reasoning with model-level attribution analysis offers robustness.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in both Instance A (13590) and Instance B (23719) and determine if any feature appears in all misclassified instances beyond these two
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features between the two instances that may be common across all misclassified inputs

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) behaves unexpectedly in terms of prediction direction despite lacking semantic relevance to income class
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis about a spurious correlation between a shared feature and misclassification

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides per-feature importance scores that can reveal which columns drive predictions in misclassified instances, especially when evaluated in intersection mode to find features highly impactful across both cases. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to confirm how these features influence outputs. Sensitivity analysis isolates the effect of each feature by ablation, helping to determine whether feature presence directly causes misclassification. Together, these tools validate the spurious nature of shared features that appear in all misclassified inputs but lack semantic relevance to income prediction.
